# character-asset-generation

Generate visual representations (headshots/avatars) for named characters who appear in the video.

**Conditional:** Only invoked when named characters were detected in `resources/brief-summary.md` by `resource-intake`. If no characters were detected, skip this skill entirely and proceed directly to `scene-author`.

**The raster exception.** Almost everything in a HyperFrames composition is vector (HTML/CSS/SVG). Character headshots are the deliberate exception — they are PNG images, generated by an image model, used as `<img>` elements in the relevant scenes. This is the only category of raster asset the agent treats as a final scene asset (alongside any supplied brand imagery / photography).

## Inputs required

- Character definitions from `resources/brief-summary.md` (name + role)
- `SCENE-PLAN.md` (to understand what context each character appears in — e.g. "Marcus appears in seq03 video-call scene and seq07 review scene")
- `design.md` (for any character styling consistency — colour wash, framing convention)

## Steps

1. **Build the character roster.** For each character in `brief-summary.md`, gather:
   - Name
   - Role / professional context (e.g. "Compliance officer at a mid-sized bank")
   - Scenes they appear in (from `SCENE-PLAN.md`)
   - Any physical description hints from the brief (age range, build, style — only what the brief actually says; do not invent details from stereotypes)

2. **Write an image prompt for each character.** Structure each prompt to produce a consistent, neutral-professional headshot that works across multiple scene contexts:

   ```
   Professional headshot of [name], [role description from brief].
   [Physical description if specified in brief, otherwise: "appearing professional and engaged"].
   Expression: neutral-professional, slight smile, eyes engaged with viewer.
   Framing: head and shoulders, square crop, centred.
   Background: clean neutral [colour from design.md surface tokens], slight depth-of-field blur.
   Lighting: soft, even, professional studio lighting.
   Style: photorealistic, modern editorial portrait, sharp focus on face.
   Format: square 800×800 PNG, no text or watermarks.
   ```

   Tailor the framing language to match the project's visual style from `design.md` — formal corporate vs. friendly startup vs. cinematic, etc.

3. **Save all prompts to `resources/character-prompts.md`** before generation. Format:

   ```markdown
   # Character image prompts

   ## Marcus — Compliance Officer
   **Scenes:** seq03-marcus-video-call, seq07-marcus-review-summary
   **Filename target:** resources/characters/marcus.png

   **Prompt:**
   [Full prompt text]

   ## [Next character]
   ...
   ```

   This file exists so prompts can be re-run if a generated image doesn't work.

4. **Generation — v1 (human-assisted).** Present the prompts to the human:

   > "I've written image prompts for [N] characters. In ChatGPT (gpt-image), Midjourney, or DALL-E, generate each one and drop the resulting PNGs into `resources/characters/[name].png` (lowercase, kebab-case name). When you're done, tell me and I'll validate them."

   Wait for the human to drop the files in.

5. **Generation — v2 (API-native, target).** When the image-generation API is wired up:
   - Call the image API directly with each prompt.
   - Receive the PNG, save to `resources/characters/[name].png`.
   - Skip the human handoff entirely.

6. **Validate received images.** For each file in `resources/characters/`:
   - Check the file exists at the expected path.
   - Check dimensions are square and ≥400px on each side (800×800 preferred).
   - Check the file is a valid PNG (`file resources/characters/marcus.png`).
   - Briefly inspect the image with multimodal vision — does it match the role described in the brief? Is the framing usable in the scene contexts it'll appear in? If something looks off (wrong age range, wrong gender presentation, distracting background), flag it to the human and offer to revise the prompt.

7. **Register each image in `resources/asset-manifest.json`** with its character associations:

   ```json
   {
     "type": "character",
     "name": "Marcus",
     "filename": "characters/marcus.png",
     "dimensions": "800x800",
     "scenes": ["seq03-marcus-video-call", "seq07-marcus-review-summary"],
     "generated_via": "human-assisted-chatgpt" | "image-api",
     "prompt_ref": "resources/character-prompts.md#marcus"
   }
   ```

8. **Background removal (optional).** If a character image needs to be composited over a vector background in a scene (rather than shown as a framed thumbnail), invoke `/hyperframes-media` and use its `remove-background` tool (u2net) to produce a transparent-background version: `resources/characters/[name]-cutout.png`. Register the cutout alongside the original in the manifest. Default behaviour is to keep the original with its neutral background unless `scene-author` calls for a cutout.

## Outputs

- `resources/characters/[character-name].png` — one per character (lowercase kebab-case)
- `resources/characters/[character-name]-cutout.png` — optional, if background removal needed
- `resources/character-prompts.md` — image prompts used (for reproducibility / regeneration)
- Updated `resources/asset-manifest.json` with character entries

## Tools used

`Read`, `Write`; image generation API (v2 — not yet wired); `/hyperframes-media` for optional `remove-background` (u2net); `Bash` for file validation (`file`, `identify` if ImageMagick available).

## Success criteria

- All characters detected in `brief-summary.md` have corresponding image files in `resources/characters/`.
- All images are valid PNGs, square, ≥400px per side.
- All images registered in `asset-manifest.json` with scene associations.
- `character-prompts.md` exists with the exact prompt for each character (so any can be regenerated without rewriting).
- The human has visually approved each character image (a quick "looks right" check, not an extensive review).
